html:
Irene of Athens was a Byzantine empress who ruled in her own name from 797 to 802, the first woman to do so. Born into a noble family of Athens around 752, she married the future emperor Leo IV in 769.

After Leo died in 780 she became regent for their nine-year-old son, Constantine VI. She ended the first period of iconoclasm by calling the Second Council of Nicaea in 787, which restored the honouring of icons. Mother and son fought for power for years. In 797 she had him blinded in the purple room of the palace where he had been born, and he died of his wounds.

In the West some argued that the imperial throne was empty while a woman held it, and on Christmas Day 800 Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor in Rome. There was even talk of a marriage between Irene and Charlemagne. In 802 her finance minister Nikephoros overthrew her, and she died in exile on Lesbos in 803.
